# infrawrench_scorecard (Resource)

A scorecard: how well each `infrawrench_service` meets the organization's own operational bar. It is a weighted list of `check` blocks ("has an on-call schedule", "no critical posture findings") and a ladder of `level` blocks (bronze, silver, gold).

Every hour each service the scorecard applies to is scored: the weight of passing checks over the weight of applicable ones, as a percentage, and the highest level whose `min_score` that reaches. A check with nothing to judge (no budget set, no stateful members to back up) is not applicable and leaves the denominator, so a stateless service is not marked down for lacking restore drills. When `alert_on_level_drop` is set, a service dropping a level raises a `scorecardAlerts` alert through `infrawrench_alert_routing`.

Every organization is seeded, once, with a "Production readiness" scorecard (`is_default`). Names are unique, so creating one under that name fails; import the seeded one to manage it here, or delete it (it is not seeded again).

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The bar for customer-facing services: tier 1 and 2 only.
resource "infrawrench_scorecard" "critical" {
  name             = "Critical service readiness"
  description      = "What every tier 1 and tier 2 service needs before launch."
  applicable_tiers = [1, 2]

  check {
    type   = "has_owner"
    weight = 2
  }
  check {
    type   = "has_on_call"
    weight = 3
  }
  check {
    type                         = "slo_within_budget"
    weight                       = 3
    min_budget_remaining_percent = 10
  }
  check {
    type              = "backups_verified"
    weight            = 2
    drill_within_days = 30
  }
  check {
    type       = "no_critical_posture"
    weight     = 2
    severities = ["critical", "high"]
  }
  check {
    type = "required_tags"
    name = "Cost allocation tags"
    tags = ["team", "cost-centre"]
  }

  # Lowest first.
  level {
    key       = "bronze"
    name      = "Bronze"
    min_score = 50
    color     = "#b0793e"
  }
  level {
    key       = "silver"
    name      = "Silver"
    min_score = 75
    color     = "#9aa4ad"
  }
  level {
    key       = "gold"
    name      = "Gold"
    min_score = 90
    color     = "#d4a72c"
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Unique in the organization; 1–120 characters.

### Optional

- `alert_on_level_drop` (Boolean) Route a `scorecardAlerts` alert when a service drops a level. Defaults to `true`.
- `applicable_tiers` (Set of Number) Service tiers (each 1–4) the scorecard applies to. Empty, the default, means every service, tiered or not; otherwise untiered services are skipped.
- `check` (Block List) A weighted check, 1–30 of them. Order is display order. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--check))
- `description` (String) What the scorecard measures; 1–1000 characters.
- `enabled` (Boolean) A disabled scorecard scores nothing and raises no alerts. Defaults to `true`.
- `level` (Block List) A rung of the ladder, 1–6 of them, written **lowest `min_score` first** (the server stores them in that order, so any other order would diff forever). A service reaches the highest level whose `min_score` its score meets; below the lowest it has no level. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--level))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Server-assigned scorecard id. Use it with `terraform import`.
- `is_default` (Boolean) Whether this is the scorecard seeded for the organization. It is still editable and deletable.

<a id="nestedblock--check"></a>
### Nested Schema for `check`

Required:

- `type` (String) The check, one of `has_owner`, `has_on_call`, `slo_within_budget`, `has_runbook`, `backups_verified`, `no_critical_posture`, `no_orphans`, `required_tags`, `cost_within_budget`, `no_critical_vulnerabilities`, `change_failure_rate`. `has_owner`: an owning team or member. `has_on_call`: an enabled on-call schedule. `slo_within_budget`: at least one linked SLO, each with enough error budget left. `has_runbook`: at least one enabled runbook. `backups_verified`: every stateful member backed up within policy with a recent passing restore drill. `no_critical_posture`: no open posture finding at the chosen severities. `no_orphans`: no member flagged as orphaned. `required_tags`: every taggable member carries the required tags. `cost_within_budget`: the last 30 days of member spend within the service's `monthly_budget`. `no_critical_vulnerabilities`: no running member has an open (not dismissed) vulnerability at the chosen severities; not applicable until a vulnerability scanner has reported. `change_failure_rate`: the service's DORA change failure rate over the window is at or under the threshold; not applicable when it shipped no production change in that window.

Optional:

- `drill_within_days` (Number) How recent the last verified restore drill must be, in days, 1–730 (default `90`). Only on `backups_verified` checks. Optional and computed: omit it for the type's default, which the server fills in and state then records.
- `id` (String) Stable id within the scorecard; results and score history refer to it, so changing it starts the check's history afresh. Omit it to use the check's `type` (then `<type>_2`, `<type>_3` for repeats, in order). Set it explicitly when the same type appears more than once and the blocks may be reordered.
- `max_failure_rate_percent` (Number) Fail when more than this share of the service's production changes failed, 0–100 (default `15`). Only on `change_failure_rate` checks. Optional and computed: omit it for the type's default, which the server fills in and state then records.
- `min_budget_remaining_percent` (Number) Fail when any linked SLO has less than this share of its error budget left, 0–100 (default `0`). Only on `slo_within_budget` checks. Optional and computed: omit it for the type's default, which the server fills in and state then records.
- `name` (String) Display name, 1–120 characters; the type's own label when omitted.
- `severities` (Set of String) Open posture findings (`no_critical_posture`, default `critical` and `high`) or open vulnerabilities on running members (`no_critical_vulnerabilities`, default `critical`) at any of these severities fail the check: any of `critical`, `high`, `medium`, `low`. Only on `no_critical_posture`, `no_critical_vulnerabilities` checks. Optional and computed: omit it for the type's default, which the server fills in and state then records.
- `tags` (Set of String) Tag keys every taggable member must carry. Empty (the default) uses the organization's tag policy (`infrawrench_tag_policy`). Only on `required_tags` checks. Optional and computed: omit it for the type's default, which the server fills in and state then records.
- `weight` (Number) How much the check counts, a whole number 1–10. Defaults to `1`.
- `window_days` (Number) How many trailing days of production changes to count, 1–90 (default `30`). Only on `change_failure_rate` checks. Optional and computed: omit it for the type's default, which the server fills in and state then records.


<a id="nestedblock--level"></a>
### Nested Schema for `level`

Required:

- `key` (String) Stable key, e.g. `gold`: lower-case letters, digits, dashes and underscores, unique within the scorecard. Alerts and score history store it, so renaming the level (`name`) does not read as a drop but changing the key does.
- `min_score` (Number) Minimum score to reach the level, 0–100; unique within the scorecard.
- `name` (String) Display name; 1–40 characters.

Optional:

- `color` (String) Six-digit hex colour for badges, e.g. `#d4a72c`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The id is in the --json output of `infrawrench scorecards`. The scorecard
# every organization is seeded with is imported the same way.
terraform import infrawrench_scorecard.example 3c4d5e6f-7a8b-4c9d-8e0f-1a2b3c4d5e6f
```
